recaps.in_short: In 1878, American orphan Tessa Gray comes to London seeking her brother Nate and is instead imprisoned by the warlock Dark Sisters, who force her to develop a rare power to transform into other people. Rescued by the Shadowhunter Will Herondale, she takes shelter at the London Institute among the Nephilim, who hunt demons and keep order over the supernatural world. There she meets the ailing, kindly Jem Carstairs and joins the effort to learn who is hunting her. The trail leads through the shadowy Pandemonium Club and the vampire De Quincey to a hidden enemy called the Magister, who is building an army of mechanical clockwork creatures. In the end the Magister is revealed to be the inventor Axel Mortmain, who has manipulated events from the start; Nate has betrayed Tessa and worked for Mortmain all along. Though De Quincey is destroyed, Mortmain escapes, having declared that Tessa herself was made for his purposes. Tessa chooses to remain at the Institute, drawn between Will and Jem, with the mystery of her own nature still unsolved.

recaps.text: Tessa Gray, a sixteen-year-old American orphan, arrives in London in 1878 to reunite with her brother Nate, only to be seized by two menacing warlock women known as the Dark Sisters. They imprison her and, through cruelty and threats, force her to uncover a strange power: by holding an object belonging to another person, she can take on that person's shape and memories. They are grooming her for a hidden master called the Magister. Tessa is rescued by a sharp-tongued young Shadowhunter, Will Herondale, one of the Nephilim who hunt demons and police the supernatural world, and is brought to the London Institute. There she is taken in by its head, Charlotte Branwell, and meets the household, including Will's gentle and gravely ill friend Jem Carstairs. Frightened and far from home, Tessa begins to grasp that she has stumbled into a hidden world, that her own gift makes her a target, and that the brother she came to save is somehow entangled in it all.

Settling uneasily at the Institute, Tessa is drawn into the Shadowhunters' investigation of who wants her and why. The Nephilim suspect the Magister works through the Pandemonium Club, a gathering of Downworlders and mundanes dabbling in dark magic, and through a powerful London vampire, De Quincey, whom they come to believe may be the Magister himself. Tessa's shape-changing gift makes her uniquely useful, and she is enlisted in a risky plan to use it to infiltrate the enemy's circle. As she trains and adjusts to Nephilim life, her feelings tangle around Will, whose cruelty and kindness alternate baffling, and Jem, whose steady warmth and hidden suffering draw her close. All the while she searches for any trace of Nate, whose fate remains unknown, and the danger closing around the Institute grows sharper.

The Shadowhunters' plans collide with the enemy. Their operation against De Quincey turns violent, and the truth about Tessa's brother surfaces: Nate is found, but he is no innocent victim. He has been in league with the Magister, and the danger he warned Tessa of was part of a scheme to deliver her into the enemy's hands. The Nephilim learn that the Magister's true weapon is not sorcery alone but machinery, an army of mechanical clockwork creatures being assembled to serve him. As betrayals come to light and the identity of the mastermind still hides just out of reach, the Institute prepares for a direct confrontation, and Tessa realizes how completely she has been used.

The Magister is unmasked as Axel Mortmain, a wealthy mundane inventor with deep occult knowledge who has directed events from behind the scenes, using the Dark Sisters and the vampire De Quincey as his instruments. The Nephilim destroy De Quincey and his followers, but he was never the true master, and Mortmain slips away with his clockwork army intact. Nate is fully exposed as a willing traitor who faked his own peril and served Mortmain, and he is left disgraced. Mortmain declares that Tessa is no ordinary person but something deliberately made, and that he intended her for himself, deepening the mystery of what she really is. Rather than flee, Tessa chooses to stay at the London Institute, accepted among the Shadowhunters. She is left caught between the guarded, self-punishing Will and the gentle, ailing Jem, both of whom have come to matter to her, while Mortmain remains at large and the threat to her is far from over.

characters.description: An American girl of sixteen, stranded in London and living at the London Institute among Shadowhunters. She can Change: holding an object that belonged to someone, she takes on that person's shape and can reach their thoughts and memories, an ability she has no explanation for. Her aunt is dead, her brother has betrayed her, and the mundane inventor who wants her is still at large, so the Institute is both refuge and the only place working against him. Bookish and stubborn, she reads her way through the Institute library, insists on being useful to the search rather than protected from it, and finds herself caught between Will Herondale, who has turned deliberately cold toward her, and his gravely ill parabatai Jem Carstairs, who has not.
characters.name: Tessa Gray

characters.description: A seventeen-year-old Shadowhunter of the London Institute, Welsh by birth, who came to the Institute as a boy and has not seen his family since. He is a gifted, reckless fighter with a cruel and quotable tongue, given to drinking, gambling and disappearing at night, and he works hard at being disliked. He was the one who pulled Tessa out of the Dark Sisters' house and has been distant and insulting to her ever since. Only Jem Carstairs, his parabatai, is allowed close to him, and even Jem does not know what Will is hiding or why he goes out alone.
characters.name: Will Herondale

characters.description: Will's parabatai, a Shadowhunter of the same age whose parents were killed in front of him in Shanghai by a demon that forced a drug on him. The drug turned his hair and eyes silver, keeps him alive, and is slowly killing him; without it he would die within days, and each dose shortens what is left. He is gentle, patient and clear-eyed where Will is destructive, plays the violin, and is the person the whole household relies on to make Will bearable. He is openly fond of Tessa. His supply of the drug is becoming harder and more expensive to obtain.
characters.name: Jem Carstairs

characters.description: Head of the London Institute, a small, determined woman in her twenties who inherited the post from her father and has been fighting for the Clave's respect ever since. She runs the household, its accounts and its investigations, takes in strays such as Tessa and Sophie, and is held responsible by the Clave for the disaster of Mortmain's escape. Her authority over the Institute is formally challenged at the start of the book, and she is given a deadline to produce results.
characters.name: Charlotte Branwell

characters.description: Charlotte's husband, an inventor who spends most of his time in the Institute crypt building devices that tend to explode. Amiable and easily distracted, he is devoted to Charlotte but frequently forgets meetings, meals and the Clave entirely. His gadgets are treated as a joke by the household, though some of them work.
characters.name: Henry Branwell

characters.description: A Shadowhunter girl raised at the Institute after her parents' deaths, who wants nothing to do with demon hunting. She refuses to train, dresses for a London society she is not part of, and talks constantly of marrying an ordinary man and living an ordinary life in an ordinary house. She resents Tessa's arrival and is barely civil to most of the household.
characters.name: Jessamine Lovelace

characters.description: A maid at the Institute, formerly a mundane servant in a grand house, dismissed and scarred across the face by an employer's son. Charlotte took her in and she is fiercely loyal in return, especially to Tessa, whom she serves and befriends. She has no patience for Will. Along with the other women of the household she is put into weapons training when the Lightwood brothers arrive as instructors.
characters.name: Sophie Collins

characters.description: Tessa's older brother, who wrote to her from London and whose letters brought her to England. He proved to be working for Mortmain, sold her to the Dark Sisters, and betrayed the Institute from inside, and he has been in hiding ever since. Charming, self-pitying and entirely self-interested, he is the one thread the Institute has back to the man they are hunting.
characters.name: Nate Gray

characters.description: A mundane businessman and inventor who built an army of clockwork automatons animated by bound demon energies and who tried to have Tessa delivered to him as a bride. He escaped the Institute's trap and has vanished, leaving the Clave without a single confirmed address for him. He hates Shadowhunters with a patience that suggests a reason, he claims to know exactly what Tessa is, and he seems to have known the Institute's business from the inside.
characters.name: Axel Mortmain

characters.description: Head of a wealthy London Shadowhunter family and a member of the Council, cold and correct in manner and long convinced that the London Institute should have been his. He presses the Clave to remove Charlotte from her post and sends his two sons to the Institute as instructors, which everyone understands is also a way of watching her.
characters.name: Benedict Lightwood

characters.description: Benedict Lightwood's younger son, close in age to Will and openly hostile to him over an old quarrel involving Gabriel's sister. Quick-tempered and eager to prove himself, he arrives at the Institute as a training instructor on his father's orders and makes no secret of thinking little of the place.
characters.name: Gabriel Lightwood

characters.description: Benedict Lightwood's elder son, recently returned from several years at the Madrid Institute. Reserved, formal and much steadier than his brother, he is sent to train the women of the Institute household and takes the work seriously, particularly Sophie's. He is plainly uncomfortable about his father's dealings and says less than he knows.
characters.name: Gideon Lightwood

characters.description: A warlock of London, centuries old, with slit-pupilled cat's eyes and an appetite for parties, colour and expensive things. He is one of the few Downworlders who will deal with the Institute, acts as go-between for the vampire Camille Belcourt, and agrees to help Will with a private matter of his own for a price. Under the flippancy he is capable, well-informed and unusually kind.
characters.name: Magnus Bane

characters.description: A vampire of London, once second to the clan leader the Shadowhunters destroyed, elegant and entirely transactional. She claims to know something about Mortmain and is willing to trade it, but she negotiates through Magnus Bane and expects a pardon and the Institute's protection in return. Nothing she offers comes without a condition attached.
characters.name: Camille Belcourt

characters.description: The elderly, retired head of the York Institute, suspicious of strangers and contemptuous of the London Institute and its young mistress. He kept meticulous records and trophies of his own hunts, including a raid decades ago that the London Shadowhunters now need to know about, and he guards both his archive and his family's private grief.
characters.name: Aloysius Starkweather

characters.description: The Consul, the highest elected office of the Clave, a large and imposing former Shadowhunter who knew Charlotte's father and treats her as a girl playing at his old friend's job. He grants her a fortnight to produce Mortmain and makes clear that Benedict Lightwood is waiting to take the Institute if she fails.
characters.name: Josiah Wayland

characters.description: Will's younger sister, who arrives at the Institute alone at the end of the book and demands to be trained as a Shadowhunter. She has not seen her brother since he left home as a boy, she is as stubborn and as sharp-tongued as he is, and she has come with the intention of bringing him back to their family.
characters.name: Cecily Herondale

recaps.ending: Mortmain's reach extends into the Institute itself: Nate Gray is fatally injured by one of the clockwork creatures and dies in Tessa's arms, leaving only fragments of what he knew. Charlotte uncovers proof that the Consul, Josiah Wayland, has been passing information to Mortmain from the Clave's highest office, confronts him with it, and keeps the Institute. Benedict Lightwood withdraws his claim rather than have his demon pox and his payments from Mortmain made public; his elder son Gideon leaves the family house for the Institute, where Sophie's regard for him is returned. Charlotte tells Henry that she is expecting a child. Jessamine remains in the Silent City. Tessa is engaged to Jem, who is dying and whose supply of the drug that sustains him is increasingly precarious. Will, having learned that the curse he built his life around never existed, tells Tessa he loves her, discovers he is too late, and says nothing further out of loyalty to his parabatai, so the three of them go on together with it unspoken. Mortmain is still free, with his automaton army, the Pyxis taken from the Institute, and an unexplained purpose for Tessa. The book closes with a girl at the Institute door: Cecily, Will's younger sister, come to take him home and refusing to leave without him.
recaps.in_short: London, 1878. Tessa Gray is living at the London Institute while the Clave gives Charlotte Branwell a fortnight to find the vanished inventor Axel Mortmain or forfeit the Institute to Benedict Lightwood. The search produces Mortmain's history rather than his address: he was the adopted mundane son of two warlocks killed in a Shadowhunter raid, and has spent his life building an automaton army to avenge them. Jessamine Lovelace is exposed as having fed information to Tessa's traitor brother Nate and is taken to the Silent City. Will Herondale, who has believed since he was twelve that a demon cursed everyone who loves him, forces that demon to admit it lied, and is freed just as Tessa accepts a proposal from his dying parabatai, Jem Carstairs. Benedict's claim on the Institute collapses when his demon pox and his dealings with Mortmain surface, and Charlotte holds her post after discovering that the Consul himself has been Mortmain's informant. Nate dies of his injuries in Tessa's arms, Mortmain remains at large, and Will's sister Cecily arrives at the Institute demanding to be trained.

recaps.text: Previously, in Clockwork Angel: in 1878 Tessa Gray sailed from New York to London to join her brother Nathaniel after her aunt's death. She was met instead by the Dark Sisters, two warlocks who imprisoned her and forced her to discover that she could Change, taking another person's shape by holding something of theirs and reaching their thoughts and memories. They told her she was being prepared for a man called the Magister, who meant to marry her. Will Herondale, a Shadowhunter of the London Institute, got her out, and she was taken into the Institute household: its head Charlotte Branwell and her inventor husband Henry, the resentful Jessamine Lovelace, the scarred maid Sophie, and Will's parabatai Jem Carstairs, kept alive by a demon drug that is also killing him. The hunt for the Magister led them to a vampire's house and to an army of clockwork automatons animated by bound demon energies. The Magister proved to be Axel Mortmain, a mundane industrialist with a private grudge against Shadowhunters and a plan that requires Tessa herself. Nathaniel had been working for him throughout and betrayed the Institute from inside; two of its household were killed in the attack. Mortmain escaped, telling Tessa he had arranged her birth and knew what she was. Tessa stayed on at the Institute with no family left, wearing the small clockwork angel her mother left her, which ticks like a heart.

The Clave's patience has run out. The Consul, Josiah Wayland, gives Charlotte a fortnight to find Mortmain or lose the Institute, and Benedict Lightwood, who has wanted it for years, is ready to take it. Benedict's sons Gideon and Gabriel are installed as training instructors for the women of the household, which everyone understands is also a way of watching Charlotte. Tessa, who has no family left and no standing among Shadowhunters, insists on being part of the search rather than kept out of it. Will is colder and more reckless than in the previous book and refuses to explain his nights away from the Institute to anyone, including Jem, whose illness is worsening and whose drug supply is becoming harder to obtain. The one lead available is Camille Belcourt, a vampire who was second to the clan leader the Shadowhunters destroyed; she claims to know something of Mortmain and will trade it, negotiating through the warlock Magnus Bane, for a pardon and the Institute's protection.

Camille's terms are agreed, and what she gives points the Institute north. Mortmain's history runs back to a pair of warlocks named Shade, who built mechanical creatures and raised a mundane boy as their son. Charlotte, Will and Tessa travel to York to see Aloysius Starkweather, the old and hostile former head of the York Institute, who led the raid that destroyed the Shades decades ago and kept records of it. Using an object from his collection Tessa Changes and lives through that raid from inside another person's memory: Shadowhunters killing the warlock household, and the boy they had raised surviving it. That boy was Axel Mortmain, and his war on the Nephilim is a revenge he has spent a lifetime preparing. Starkweather's family carries a private grief of its own, a granddaughter who died the first time she was Marked, which suggests his bloodline was not what the Clave believed. Meanwhile Will is pursuing something of his own with Magnus Bane's help, vanishing at night and refusing to say why, leaving Jem to cover for him.

Jessamine has been leaving the Institute at night in disguise. She is followed and caught: she has been meeting Nate Gray, who has promised her marriage and the ordinary mundane life she has always wanted, and she has been passing him what she learns at the Institute. Questioned by the Silent Brothers under the Mortal Sword, which compels the truth, she gives up what she knows and is taken to the Silent City, and the household learns that Mortmain's real object inside the Institute was the Pyxis, the sealed box of bound demon energies he needs to animate his automatons. Nate is taken into custody. Around this the household's private lives tighten: Sophie is drawn to Gideon Lightwood, who is increasingly ashamed of his father and says less than he knows; Jem's health continues to slip; and Will, still working with Magnus Bane, is hunting a specific demon for reasons he will not explain to anyone.

Jem tells Tessa that he loves her and asks her to marry him, knowing what his illness means, and she accepts; he gives her his mother's jade pendant. Will's private hunt is finally explained. When he was twelve he opened a Pyxis in his father's study and released a demon, Marbas, which told him that from then on anyone who loved him would die. His older sister died that same night. Believing it, he ran from his family to the Institute and has spent five years making himself unlovable on purpose, which is the whole of his cruelty toward Tessa and his distance from everyone else. With Magnus Bane's help he summons and binds Marbas, which admits there was never a curse at all: it had frightened a child with a lie and killed his sister to make the lie hold. Will comes back free to love and be loved for the first time since he was a boy, and finds Tessa engaged to his parabatai.

Will's long-mocked insistence that demon pox is real turns out to matter. Benedict Lightwood has the disease, contracted through years of consorting with demons, and Will and Magnus see the proof at a demon revel held at Benedict's own house. Gideon, who has broken with his father, supplies the rest: Benedict has been taking Mortmain's money, which is why he pushed so hard for the Institute. Faced with exposure, Benedict withdraws his claim; Gideon leaves for the Institute while Gabriel stays behind with their father. Charlotte's fortnight is almost spent and the investigation has produced a history rather than an address. Mortmain is a mundane raised by warlocks the Nephilim killed, he holds property under names that are not his, and he has consistently known Institute business that no outsider should know, which points at someone inside the Clave.

Mortmain reaches inside the Institute one last time: Nate Gray is fatally injured by one of the clockwork creatures and dies in Tessa's arms. Charlotte uncovers correspondence proving that the Consul, Josiah Wayland, has been supplying Mortmain with information from the Clave's highest office, confronts him, and keeps the Institute; Benedict Lightwood's claim collapses, Gideon settles at the Institute for good, and Sophie's feeling for him is returned. Charlotte tells Henry she is expecting a child. Tessa is engaged to Jem, who is dying and knows it. Will, freed from a curse that never existed, tells Tessa he loves her, learns he is too late, and chooses silence and his parabatai's happiness over his own. Mortmain remains at large with his automaton army, the stolen Pyxis and an unexplained use for Tessa, and the Clave's own leadership has been compromised. In the closing pages a girl arrives at the Institute door demanding to be trained as a Shadowhunter: Cecily, Will's younger sister, come to bring him home.

characters.description: A young American woman living at the London Institute, able to Change into another person by holding something that belonged to them and to reach that person's thoughts and memories. She is engaged to Jem Carstairs, whose illness is worsening, and she is still the object of Axel Mortmain's plans, which no one at the Institute understands. She has no family left, no legal standing among Shadowhunters, and no clear idea of what she is; she wears a small clockwork angel that belonged to her mother and that ticks like a heart. She loves Jem and has never resolved what she feels for his parabatai, Will Herondale.
characters.name: Tessa Gray

characters.description: A Shadowhunter of the London Institute, Welsh by birth, released at the end of the previous book from a childhood belief that everyone who loved him would die. Free to feel and to be loved for the first time in five years, he finds that Tessa is promised to Jem, his parabatai and the person he loves most in the world, and he has chosen to say nothing further about it. His sister Cecily is now living at the Institute and trying to persuade him to come home. He is a formidable fighter, still reckless, and no longer performing cruelty for anyone's benefit.
characters.name: Will Herondale

characters.description: Will's parabatai and Tessa's fiance, kept alive by a demon drug that is also killing him. The drug turned his hair and eyes silver and the doses that sustain him shorten what is left of his life. He is patient, generous and clear-sighted, plays the violin, and is the steadying centre of the household. He and Tessa are planning their wedding against the clock: his supply of the drug has become nearly impossible to obtain, and everyone in the Institute knows what that means.
characters.name: Jem Carstairs

characters.description: Head of the London Institute, who held her post against Benedict Lightwood's challenge and is now expecting her first child while running the household, its investigations and its dealings with a Clave whose leadership she knows to be compromised. She is practical, tenacious and protective of everyone under her roof, including those the Clave would not count as hers.
characters.name: Charlotte Branwell

characters.description: Charlotte's husband, an inventor who works in the Institute crypt on devices most of the household treats as a joke. Cheerful, forgetful and entirely devoted to Charlotte, he is more useful than anyone expects when the Institute needs equipment that does not exist yet.
characters.name: Henry Branwell

characters.description: Formerly a mundane maid at the Institute, scarred by a previous employer's son and taken in by Charlotte. She is now training in earnest with the household's weapons, is trusted as a member of it rather than a servant, and is attached to Gideon Lightwood, a Shadowhunter, which is a difficult thing for a mundane woman to be.
characters.name: Sophie Collins

characters.description: Will's younger sister, living at the Institute and training as a Shadowhunter after arriving alone at its door. She came to bring Will home to their parents in Wales and has stayed instead, learning the work from scratch as an adult among people who began as children. She is as stubborn and as sharp as her brother, resents being treated as a novice, and finds herself increasingly interested in Gabriel Lightwood.
characters.name: Cecily Herondale

characters.description: Benedict Lightwood's elder son, who broke with his father and moved into the Institute. Reserved and dependable, he trains the household's women, is quietly in love with Sophie, and carries the shame of what his family has done.
characters.name: Gideon Lightwood

characters.description: Benedict Lightwood's younger son, who stayed with his father when his brother left and is increasingly unable to explain or excuse what is happening at the family house. Proud, quick-tempered and out of his depth, he has an old feud with Will and a growing interest in Will's sister Cecily.
characters.name: Gabriel Lightwood

characters.description: A mundane inventor and industrialist with an army of clockwork automatons animated by bound demon energies, still at large after the Institute failed twice to take him. He was raised by warlocks whom Shadowhunters killed, and his war on the Nephilim is a revenge he has spent his life preparing. He wants Tessa Gray, claims to have arranged her birth, and has enough reach into ordinary commerce to control what the Institute can buy.
characters.name: Axel Mortmain

characters.description: Head of the Lightwood family, forced to withdraw his claim on the Institute after his dealings with Mortmain and his demon pox came to light. He has shut himself up in his house, refuses visitors, and is deteriorating in ways his sons cannot manage or explain.
characters.name: Benedict Lightwood

characters.description: A Shadowhunter girl raised at the Institute, returned to it from the Silent City under confinement after passing information to Mortmain's agent, the man she believed would marry her and take her away from Shadowhunter life. She is frightened, diminished and kept apart from the household, and no one is certain how far she can be trusted.
characters.name: Jessamine Lovelace

characters.description: A servant taken on at the Institute who turns out to be an extraordinary fighter and a considerable asset in the armoury. She sings long, bloody ballads about murder and betrayal while she works, to the household's general discomfort.
characters.name: Bridget Daly

characters.description: A centuries-old warlock of London, extravagant, well-connected and one of the few Downworlders who will work with the Institute. He helped Will in the previous book, knows more about Mortmain's kind of magic than the Nephilim do, and is the person the household turns to when the problem is not one a blade solves.
characters.name: Magnus Bane

characters.description: Head of the London werewolf pack, fastidious, theatrical and openly uninterested in Shadowhunter opinion. He is Magnus Bane's lover, and the Institute has reason to want both his information and his goodwill.
characters.name: Woolsey Scott

recaps.ending: Cornered in Mortmain's stronghold beneath Cadair Idris, Tessa discovers what her mother's clockwork angel is: an angel, Ithuriel, bound inside it, whose life has been sustaining and healing her since birth. She takes the angel's own shape and uses its power to destroy Mortmain and burn out his automaton army, ending the threat and freeing the angel. Henry is crippled in the battle and will not walk again, and the parabatai bond between Will and Jem breaks during the fight. Jem is not dead: dying and out of the drug that sustained him, he was taken by the Silent Brothers and survived the transformation into one of them, and he returns as Brother Zachariah, no longer able to marry Tessa or to live as James Carstairs. Will and Tessa, who turned to each other in grief, marry with Jem's blessing and have two children, James and Lucie. Charlotte becomes Consul; Sophie Ascends and marries Gideon; Cecily marries Gabriel. Will lives a full life and dies an old man with Tessa and Jem beside him, and Tessa, who does not age, outlives them all. The book closes in the present day on Blackfriars Bridge, where Tessa keeps a standing appointment with Jem, still a Silent Brother, once a year, and where the two of them are still waiting for a change that might one day give them back to each other.
recaps.in_short: Tessa Gray and Jem Carstairs plan their wedding while Axel Mortmain quietly buys up the drug keeping Jem alive, and Benedict Lightwood's demon pox turns him into a monster his own sons must destroy. Mortmain's agents reach into the Institute, Jessamine Lovelace is killed, and Tessa is carried off to his stronghold beneath the Welsh mountain Cadair Idris. Will Herondale rides for Wales alone and the household follows; Jem, out of his drug and dying, is left behind, and during the pursuit Will feels their parabatai bond break. Mortmain tells Tessa what she is: the deliberately engineered child of a Shadowhunter mother and a Greater Demon that took the body of her mother's husband, made shapeshifter, fertile, and unmarked, to be his bride and the mother of a new race. Cornered, Tessa takes the shape of the angel bound inside her mother's clockwork pendant and destroys Mortmain and his automaton army. Jem is not dead; he survived by becoming a Silent Brother. Will and Tessa marry and have children, Will dies of old age with both of them beside him, and the story ends more than a century later with Tessa and Jem meeting on Blackfriars Bridge.

recaps.text: Previously in The Infernal Devices: Tessa Gray came from New York to London in 1878, was imprisoned by two warlocks who forced her to discover that she can Change into anyone whose possession she holds, and was rescued by Will Herondale of the London Institute. She has lived there since, among Charlotte and Henry Branwell, the maid Sophie, Jessamine Lovelace and Will's parabatai Jem Carstairs, who is kept alive and slowly killed by a demon drug. Her brother Nate betrayed her and the Institute to Axel Mortmain, a mundane inventor with an army of clockwork automatons who wants Tessa for reasons of his own; Nate died of his injuries in Tessa's arms. Mortmain was raised by warlocks killed in a Shadowhunter raid and has spent his life preparing revenge on the Nephilim, and he escaped both attempts to take him, with a stolen box of bound demon energies. Charlotte kept the Institute against Benedict Lightwood's challenge after his demon pox and his payments from Mortmain came to light, and after discovering that the Consul himself had been Mortmain's informant. Will learned that the demon who told him as a child that everyone who loved him would die had lied, freeing him five years too late: Tessa had just accepted a proposal from the dying Jem, and Will said nothing. Will's sister Cecily arrived at the Institute demanding to be trained.

Tessa and Jem are engaged and their wedding is being arranged, but the drug that keeps Jem alive has become impossible to buy: Mortmain has been quietly acquiring the entire supply, so that Jem's death is now a matter of weeks and is in Mortmain's gift. Will, who says nothing about his own feelings, spends his time hunting for a source anywhere in Britain. Cecily Herondale is training at the Institute and still trying to make her brother come home to Wales; Gideon Lightwood is living there too, close to Sophie; Gabriel remains at the family house, where Benedict has shut himself away, refuses to be seen, and is behaving in ways his sons cannot explain. Charlotte, expecting a child, runs the Institute and its search knowing that the Clave's own leadership has been compromised. Nobody has found Mortmain, who has no fixed address, several false names, and the ability to reach the Institute's household without being seen.

Gabriel arrives at the Institute for help: his father's demon pox has run its course and Benedict Lightwood is no longer a man but a monstrous creature loose on the family estate. The Shadowhunters go to the house and destroy it, and both Lightwood brothers move into the Institute for good, their family name in ruins. Jessamine Lovelace is released from the Silent City into the Institute's custody, frightened and much reduced, kept apart from the household and trusted by no one. The Institute's defences are tested by Mortmain's automatons, which are better made than the ones the Shadowhunters have fought before, and it becomes plain that what Mortmain wants in exchange for leaving them alone is Tessa herself. Charlotte refuses to consider it. Jem's condition continues to worsen, and the wedding is brought forward against the certainty that time is running out.

Mortmain reaches inside the Institute. Jessamine, manipulated and coerced, is used to get his creatures past its protections, and she is killed for what she does or fails to do; the household finds her too late to save her. In the same stroke Tessa is taken out of the Institute and carried away, and every search the Shadowhunters mount for her fails, because Mortmain's stronghold is not in London and is not on any map the Clave holds. Jem, out of the drug that sustains him and told that Tessa is gone, deteriorates sharply. The Institute pieces together, from Mortmain's history, his properties and the fragments Nate and Jessamine left behind, that the place they are looking for is in Wales, under the mountain Cadair Idris.

Will rides for Wales alone the moment the location is known, refusing to wait for the Clave and riding almost without rest. Jem, too ill to follow, is left in the Institute's care as the last of his drug runs out; the Silent Brothers take him, and the household expects him to die. Charlotte, Henry, Cecily, Gideon, Gabriel and Sophie follow Will west with what weapons Henry can devise. In Mortmain's stronghold beneath the mountain, Tessa is held in comfort and dressed for a wedding: Mortmain intends to marry her, and he has a use for her that goes beyond the marriage. He begins to tell her, in pieces, what she is and why she exists, and it becomes clear that her ability to Change and her lack of a warlock's mark were designed rather than accidental.

Mortmain gives Tessa the whole of it. Her birth was engineered: her mother was of Shadowhunter blood, and her father was a Greater Demon that Mortmain summoned into the body of her mother's husband, so that the child would be a shapeshifter without a warlock's mark and, unlike a warlock, able to bear children. She was made to be his bride and the beginning of a race of his own, and her brother Nate, an ordinary human child of the same marriage, was never any relation to that plan. On the road west Will feels the parabatai bond tear, and believes Jem has died. He reaches the mountain ahead of the others and gets to Tessa, and the two of them, grieving Jem and expecting to die there, admit to each other what neither has said. Mortmain's automaton army is assembled beneath Cadair Idris, and the handful of Shadowhunters converging on the mountain have no realistic chance against it.

The battle at Cadair Idris goes badly: the Shadowhunters are hopelessly outnumbered by the automatons, and Henry is struck down and crippled, losing the use of his legs. Cornered by Mortmain, Tessa finally learns what the clockwork angel her mother left her actually is. An angel, Ithuriel, is bound inside it, and its life has been keeping her alive and healing her injuries since she was born. Tessa takes the angel's own shape, the one form she has never been able to hold, and its power destroys Mortmain and burns out the mechanical army with him. The angel is freed and the pendant falls silent. The threat that has shaped all three books ends there, at the cost of Henry's legs, of Jessamine's life, and, as far as anyone at the mountain knows, of Jem's.

Jem did not die. Dying and beyond the drug's help, he was taken by the Silent Brothers and survived the transformation into one of them; he returns as Brother Zachariah, unable to marry Tessa or to live as James Carstairs, but alive and still himself enough to release them both. Will and Tessa marry with his blessing and have two children, James and Lucie. Charlotte becomes Consul; Sophie Ascends to Shadowhunter and marries Gideon; Cecily marries Gabriel; Henry works from a wheelchair for the rest of his life. Will lives to be an old man, and dies with Tessa and Jem beside him. Tessa, who does not age, outlives her husband, her friends and eventually her children. The book closes more than a century later, in the present day, on Blackfriars Bridge in London, where Tessa keeps the appointment she and Jem have kept once a year for decades: he is still a Silent Brother, she is still waiting, and the two of them go on meeting there in the hope that will one day change.

recaps.ending: Earth returns from the battles with the local Skay destroyed and Rigel driven away, but both victories are costly. Galina Turov resolves the duplicate crisis by killing one James McGill and presenting the survivor as the original. McGill later kills Sateekas to stop the torture of a copied Squanto, and Primus Graves helps conceal the act. The revived Sateekas accepts their false account and loses his fleet command. Drusus retains command, while the captured Rigelian cruiser gives Earth access to armor-piercing weapons. Etta and Florimel begin studying that technology. Drusus also plans to revive a backdated Winslade and monitor him for intelligence, while McGill asks that Lisa's saved scan receive another chance. McGill is demobilized in Georgia. Claver X arrives there with Abigail and warns that disagreement over machine intelligence and imperial succession has widened into civil war. McGill agrees to bring them to Drusus, leaving Earth with new technology and a brief respite but exposed to a larger conflict.
recaps.in_short: Financial need draws James McGill into a lethal rift mission against Rigel, where his sabotage destroys an orbital city and exposes Claver's infiltration of Earth. Legion Varus attacks Clone World, uncovers Winslade's treason, and destroys Claver's fortress, but the victory attracts both the Skay and Mogwa. Earth sides with the Mogwa, and human boarders destroy the final Skay. A delayed revival creates two McGills, so Galina Turov kills one and protects the survivor. Sateekas then forces Earth into battle with Rigel. McGill kills Sateekas during the torture of a copied Squanto, learns the secret of Rigel's armor-piercing rear line, and hides the killing with Primus Graves. McGill's cohort captures one of those cruisers, whose weapons help rout Rigel. Back on Earth, Drusus prepares a covert revival operation, while Claver X and Abigail warn McGill that an imperial civil war over machine intelligence is spreading toward Earth.

recaps.text: Previously: James McGill is a Legion Varus centurion and Etta's father. His long military career has left him tied to senior officers including Galina Turov, Drusus, and Primus Graves, as well as comrades such as Carlos, Sargon, Harris, Leeson, Natasha, and Della. Florimel works with advanced technology at Central, where Etta serves as her assistant. McGill has encountered Claver and the wider clone network before, while Earth remains subordinate to the Mogwa within a dangerous galactic order. Earlier campaigns also established the Skay as a machine-intelligence power and left McGill with connections to the mercenary Armel and the Mogwa commander Sateekas.

So far this book: Short of money while away from active service, James McGill accepts a hazardous contract at Central. Florimel's team has built an unstable rift that can place a person on Rigel but cannot bring the subject home. Revival is possible only if Central receives proof of death. After a violent first reconnaissance exposes the operation, McGill returns through the rift to sabotage the reactor of Rigel's orbital city. He finds Claver clones guarding it and Armel commanding human mercenaries there. McGill causes an irreversible containment failure, and Armel kills him in time for Central to revive him as the reactor goes critical and the city destabilizes. Before the second insertion, Claver also demonstrates that his agents operate on Earth by threatening Etta and arranging McGill's death. The mission has therefore shifted from covert reconnaissance into an open conflict involving Rigel, Claver, and compromised human security.

So far this book: Rigel offers peace in exchange for McGill's permanent death. When Deitch rejects McGill's report about Claver involvement, McGill shoots him, but the body proves to be a disguised Claver agent. An apparent Drusus is another impostor, showing that Earth's senior command has been penetrated while the real officials are missing. Earth responds to the proposed exchange by preparing an expedition against Claver's clone operation. Legion Varus departs aboard Leggett with a near-human formation. Armel has lost command of that allied legion, and Winslade unexpectedly takes the post. Carlos and Sargon suspect that his motives are concealed. McGill enters Winslade's restricted area under false pretenses, only for Winslade to mistake him for an operative sent by Claver. McGill has uncovered the edge of a conspiracy without yet knowing its membership or purpose, while the larger mission is already heading toward Claver's world.

So far this book: Winslade's alarm at references to Claver deepens McGill's suspicions, and near-human slavers attack him after he leaves the officer's area. Badly injured and worried that conspirators can alter his revival record, McGill persuades Evelyn Thompson to make a secret physical backup. His current data is then deleted, proving the danger was real. Revived from the backup but still injured, he leads a hard-vacuum exercise against Bubbles's cephalopods. Cooper and most of the unit fall in the fighting. Carlos sacrifices himself with an improvised explosive attack that kills Bubbles and breaks the opposing force, giving McGill's survivors the victory. Winslade then tries to arrest McGill, but Primus Graves produces evidence that Winslade has communicated with Earth's enemies. Galina Turov declares Winslade a traitor, Graves executes him, and McGill openly aligns with Turov against Claver. Winslade is removed, but the evidence suggests that the hostile network aboard Leggett is larger than one officer.

So far this book: Leggett's force learns that Claver has built an illegal clone army on the outer world targeted by the expedition. Galina Turov agrees with McGill that Claver probably expects their arrival and that hidden defectors remain aboard. She approaches the system in radio silence and uses a false raid plan as a leak test. Saboteurs led by the revived Bubbles breach Leggett's hull, and a large force of Claver combat clones surrounds the troops sent outside to stop them. McGill disobeys orders to hold the breach and instead leads a counterattack with gunfire and gravity weapons. The combined action kills or disperses much of the clone force and drives the remainder away, though Leeson dies in the battle. The attack confirms both internal sabotage and Claver's ability to place a substantial army against Leggett before the ship reaches the planet. The transport survives the first assault, but its mission has become an urgent battle against enemies inside and outside the hull.

So far this book: Claver fighters attack Leggett, and technical clones teleport aboard to disable its fire-control room. McGill retakes the compartment in time for the ship to launch a second barrage. Galina Turov then sends him with a commando raid against Claver's headquarters. He arrives in an ambush, helps the survivors escape, and dies alone while covering their withdrawal. Claver revives him inside the fortress and prepares to transfer him to Squanto. Toro, a former Legion Varus adjunct now directing special operations for Claver, reveals that she helped command the attack on Leggett. McGill pressures her over her own vulnerability, and she secretly stops the transfer. Toro arms him, lets him kill the guards, and asks him to shoot her so her later revival will not expose her betrayal. McGill escapes through a gateway and emerges beneath Central City, proving that Claver has a hidden route into Earth's capital. Mortally wounded, he reaches transmission range and uploads his record before dying, allowing Earth to revive him with the discovery intact.

So far this book: Revived at Central, McGill conceals Toro's role but gives Drusus enough supported information to return to the campaign. Galina Turov orders Leggett to warp into low orbit, destroy Clone World's anti-space batteries, and deploy Legion Varus before the defenses can answer. The ground force lands in radioactive terrain and penetrates an inner dome that blocks outside support and communications. Sargon destroys a concealed turret, while McGill's unit relieves Manfred's soldiers and captures Lisa, a former Legion Germanica centurion commanding Claver troops. Lisa explains that Claver replaces missing officers with cloned continuations and says his alliance includes Rigel and the Skay. Turov accepts that warning but presses the attack before the machine intelligences can arrive. With no safe way to carry a prisoner, McGill kills Lisa. During the fortress approach, Della dies destroying the center of three turrets, allowing Sargon's team to eliminate the others. Varus reaches the fortress and begins a direct assault under heavy defensive fire, with no reliable reconnaissance or external support.

So far this book: Legion Varus breaches Claver's fortress and destroys its remaining defenders, but most gateways have already been ruined and senior enemies have escaped. Claver X, a dissident who is searching for Abigail, surrenders and takes McGill through the last working portal. On Dark World, McGill sees a rebuilt shipyard capable of producing warships for Rigel. Claver X says he opposes his brothers' attempt to dominate humanity and asks McGill to pass the intelligence to Earth. Back at Clone World, long-range sensors detect Skay and Mogwa forces converging on the system. Drusus chooses to remain and gathers Earth's fleet rather than let the destruction of the clone base lead the Skay back to Earth. The arriving Skay leader demands an explanation, and McGill persuades it that Earth acted in its interest. Rigel then approaches in support of the Skay. Drusus commits humanity to the Mogwa side, and Galina Turov orders McGill's cohort to teleport into the smallest Skay as its hull opens. Earth has escaped immediate punishment only by entering a much larger battle.

So far this book: McGill's cohort boards the smallest Skay with timed teleport charges intended to guarantee death and revival. Natasha disables those timers, accepting the risk that delayed memory transfers could create duplicate soldiers, and scatters scouts in search of a critical target. McGill enters a vast internal structure while Skay defenders pursue him. Sateekas reports that two Skay have been destroyed but the final sphere has defeated most of the Mogwa fleet. McGill refuses orders to stop, reaches a central shaft, and dies without retaining the final moments. He revives aboard Drusus's flagship with his memories delayed through the Skay network. Another McGill has already been revived from the earlier record, leaving two living versions of the same man. The internal attack nevertheless destroyed the last Skay, while Leggett and much of the allied force were lost. Galina Turov kills one duplicate and directs the survivor to claim the status of the original. Sateekas then boards, accepts McGill's explanation of Earth's conduct, commandeers the surviving human fleet, and orders it to meet the approaching Rigelian force.

So far this book: Squanto reveals that Earth previously sent Rigel a copy of McGill rather than permanently surrendering the original, ending the truce. Sateekas removes Drusus and briefly puts McGill in command against a much larger Rigelian fleet. McGill prepares mass boarding attacks using missile bursts to lower enemy shields. Sateekas then commandeers Earth's revival systems and produces a backdated copy of Squanto for interrogation. When the Mogwa begins torturing the prisoner, McGill disables the live transmission and kills Sateekas. He deceives the copied Squanto into believing Rigel has already lost, learning that the rear formation carries weapons able to penetrate collapsed stardust armor. McGill then kills the copy and stages the scene to blame him for Sateekas's death. Primus Graves removes McGill from fleet command but agrees to revive Sateekas and support the false account. Drusus resumes command and assigns McGill's cohort to board the dangerous rear line once Earth's barrage creates an opening.

So far this book: McGill's cohort teleports aboard a rear-line Rigelian cruiser and captures it after costly close fighting. Leeson dies taking engineering, Erin Barton dies clearing the cargo spaces, and about half the unit is lost. Natasha establishes control and contacts Galina Turov before human missiles can destroy the prize. As Drusus's flagship fails, its surviving command staff transfers to the captured ship. Natasha and the technicians turn the cruiser's armor-piercing guns against Rigel from behind, breaking the enemy formation and forcing its surviving fleet into retreat. Earth returns home after a victory that has destroyed much of its own new fleet. The revived Sateekas, stripped of command, accepts McGill's fabricated explanation of his death. Florimel and Etta begin studying the captured weapons. Drusus plans to revive an earlier Winslade copy and watch him secretly for intelligence, while McGill asks Galina Turov to consider reviving Lisa from her saved scan. McGill is demobilized in Georgia, where Claver X and Abigail warn him that conflict over machine intelligence and imperial succession has become a wider civil war. He agrees to take them to Drusus.

characters.description: A telepathic waitress at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, Louisiana, still with Bill Compton but no longer comfortable in the relationship. Twice now she has been hurt badly for the sake of vampire business, and she has begun to price her own cooperation. She is stubborn, practical and increasingly known among the supernatural community of the region as a human worth having, which is not the same thing as being safe.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: Sookie's vampire lover, a Bon Temps native who died in the Civil War and came home more than a century later. He has been working long nights on a confidential project for the vampire hierarchy of Louisiana and will not tell Sookie what it is. He is distracted, secretive and short with her, and at the start of the book he leaves town on business he describes only vaguely.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: Sookie's boss at Merlotte's and a shapeshifter, one of the few people in Bon Temps who knows most of what she is mixed up in. He does not hide his opinion that the vampires are using her, and he gives her time off and a certain amount of cover when she needs it.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: The thousand-year-old Norse vampire who rules the vampires of northern Louisiana from his Shreveport bar, Fangtasia. Bill's disappearance is his problem as much as Sookie's, since a vampire cannot be taken out of a territory without insult to the one who holds it. He brings her the news, arranges her protection, and, as always, expects the arrangement to leave her further in his debt.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: Eric's second at Fangtasia, blonde, dry and thoroughly unsentimental, who handles the practical side of running the bar and the territory while Eric travels.
characters.name: Pam

characters.description: The vampire who made Bill Compton into what he is, and to whom he is bound by the tie between maker and child. Sookie learns of her existence only when Bill vanishes, along with the fact that Bill had been intending to leave Bon Temps and go back to her.
characters.name: Lorena Ball

characters.description: A Shreveport werewolf who runs his family's surveying company and is sent to escort Sookie to Jackson, Mississippi, because his father's gambling debts are owed to vampires. Big, dark-haired and easy-tempered, he is decent to Sookie beyond what the errand requires, and openly unhappy about being anybody's collateral.
characters.name: Alcide Herveaux

characters.description: Alcide's former lover, a shapeshifter from Jackson who has moved on to a werewolf fiance but has not finished with Alcide. She is immediately and openly hostile to Sookie, and she takes every opportunity in company to humiliate her.
characters.name: Debbie Pelt

characters.description: The vampire made from a famous singer, brain-damaged by a botched change and known to everyone by a nickname because his real name upsets him. He is sent to Jackson to help watch over Sookie, and he is as likely to cause an incident as to prevent one.
characters.name: Bubba

characters.description: A friend of Sookie's from school who now runs a dress shop in Bon Temps and who turns up in Jackson on the arm of a wealthy vampire. She is glad to see Sookie and plainly nervous about being seen with her, and she is deeper into the vampire world than Sookie realized.
characters.name: Tara Thornton

characters.description: An old, wealthy Mississippi vampire, courteous in a formal Italian-American style, who keeps Tara Thornton as his companion and pays for her comfortably. He is well connected among the vampires of Jackson.
characters.name: Franklin Mott

characters.description: The bouncer at Josephine's, the Jackson bar the supernatural community calls Club Dead. He is a goblin, squat and smoldering to the touch, and he enforces the bar's single rule, that nobody starts a fight inside, with unarguable force.
characters.name: Mr. Hob

characters.description: The vampire King of Mississippi, who rules from a walled mansion outside Jackson. Genial, immensely old and entirely ruthless, he keeps a court of vampires and a staff of werewolves, and treats other kingdoms' property as fair game when it suits him.
characters.name: Russell Edgington

characters.description: The tattooed vampire who tends bar at Fangtasia, taken on after the previous bartender's destruction. He is part of Eric's small circle in Shreveport and takes a share in the decisions about what to do while Eric is away.
characters.name: Chow

recaps.ending: Sookie gets Bill out of Russell Edgington's estate alive, having killed Lorena herself with a wooden stake when she found her torturing him. The rescue costs her nearly everything: starved and out of his mind in the trunk of the car, Bill drinks from Sookie until she is close to death and forces himself on her, and she is left too weak to stand. Debbie Pelt, who shoved her into that trunk deliberately, is broken with completely by Alcide, cast out in front of the people whose opinion she values. Sookie is healed with vampire blood and taken home. The Mississippi affair is settled between kings and sheriffs in the way vampire politics is always settled, and Russell Edgington keeps his throne. What does not survive is Sookie's relationship with Bill. She learns that he had planned to leave her for his maker before he was taken, and that the secret project he would not discuss is a database of the world's vampires, valuable enough that a king would kidnap and torture him for it. Sookie has the only copy and keeps it hidden rather than handing it over, which gives her leverage with the Queen of Louisiana and with Eric. She tells Bill they are finished. Eric, who spent the book in Jackson under a false name looking out for her, ends it with a much clearer idea of what he wants from her, and Alcide ends it free of Debbie and interested in Sookie.
recaps.in_short: Bill Compton is distant, secretive about a project for the vampire hierarchy, and then simply gone. Eric Northman tells Sookie the truth twice over: Bill had been planning to leave her for Lorena, the vampire who made him, and he has since been kidnapped and taken to Mississippi. Sookie agrees to help find him and travels to Jackson escorted by Alcide Herveaux, a werewolf whose family owes the vampires money. Posing as his girlfriend, she works the supernatural bar the locals call Club Dead, dodging Alcide's vicious ex-fiancee Debbie Pelt, is staked in the parking lot by a fanatic, and is healed by Eric, who is in Jackson under a false name. She traces Bill to the estate of Russell Edgington, the vampire King of Mississippi, who wants the database Bill has been building. Getting inside, she finds Bill chained and being tortured by Lorena, and kills Lorena. In the escape, Debbie pushes Sookie into the car trunk with a starving, deranged Bill, who nearly kills her. Sookie survives, keeps the database hidden as leverage, and ends her relationship with Bill.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse is a telepathic waitress at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, Louisiana, in a world where vampires live openly. She is in a relationship with Bill Compton, a Civil War veteran turned vampire who came back to his family's house across the cemetery from hers. In the previous two years her grandmother was murdered by a killer who was really hunting Sookie, and Sookie herself was nearly killed before she unmasked him. She has learned that her boss Sam Merlotte is a shapeshifter, that the woods hold worse things than vampires, and that maenads exist. Bill answers to Eric Northman, the thousand-year-old Norse vampire who rules the vampires of the area from his Shreveport bar and who takes a proprietary interest in Sookie's telepathy. Eric has already rented her out once, to the vampires of Dallas, where she was taken prisoner by the anti-vampire Fellowship of the Sun, nearly raped, and shaken by how readily Bill's obligations to his own kind outweighed his obligations to her. She loves Bill but no longer trusts the world he belongs to, and she has begun insisting on being paid and asked rather than used.

Bill has been working long nights on something he will not discuss, a project for the vampire authorities of Louisiana, and he has been distant with Sookie for weeks. He leaves town on vague business, and then stops answering. An intruder breaks into Sookie's house searching for Bill's work and she is nearly killed getting away from him. Eric Northman arrives with two pieces of news that arrive together. The first is that Bill had been intending to leave Sookie and go back to Lorena, the vampire who made him. The second is that Bill has been taken, snatched out of Eric's territory, and is being held somewhere in Mississippi. That is an insult to Eric as much as a crisis for Sookie, but Eric cannot simply invade another king's territory, and a human who can read minds can go where a vampire sheriff cannot. Furious, humiliated and unwilling to leave Bill to be tortured, Sookie agrees to go looking for him.

Sookie is driven to Jackson by Alcide Herveaux, a Shreveport werewolf who runs a surveying company and whose father's gambling debts are held by vampires, which is why he is available to be lent. Alcide is decent, plainspoken and irritated at being used as collateral, and the two get on. She is to pose as his girlfriend so that they can spend evenings at Josephine's, a Jackson bar for the supernatural community that its regulars call Club Dead, where she can listen to the thoughts of vampires' human hangers-on for word of Bill. Alcide's former lover Debbie Pelt is a fixture there, engaged to a werewolf and openly vicious toward Sookie. In the club Sookie also runs into Tara Thornton, an old friend from Bon Temps, on the arm of a wealthy Mississippi vampire named Franklin Mott. The bar's one law, no violence inside, is enforced by a goblin bouncer, which does nothing for the parking lot.

Outside the club Sookie is attacked and staked by a fanatic and comes very close to dying. She is saved by Eric, who has been in Jackson all along under a false name, posing as an ordinary out-of-town vampire so that he can watch over the operation without provoking the local king. Eric heals her with his blood and stays close. Bubba, the damaged vampire made from a famous singer, is also in town to help, with the usual mixed results. Piecing together what she overhears, Sookie establishes that Bill is being held by Russell Edgington, the vampire King of Mississippi, at his walled estate outside Jackson, and that what Edgington wants is the project Bill would not talk about. She also learns that Lorena is there, and that Bill is not simply a prisoner but is being tortured.

Sookie gets onto the Edgington estate while the vampires are at rest and searches the outbuildings. She finds Bill chained, burned and starving, with Lorena working on him, and when Lorena comes for her Sookie kills her with a wooden stake. She frees Bill and, with help from outside, gets him out of the grounds during a diversion, hiding him in the trunk of the car. Debbie Pelt, seizing the chance, shoves Sookie into that trunk and shuts it. Bill, starved past reason and unable to recognize her, drinks from her almost to death and forces himself on her before Eric can get the trunk open. Sookie survives, barely, and is healed with vampire blood again. Alcide, when he learns what Debbie did, casts her out in front of the people whose good opinion she lives on and is finished with her for good.

Recovering, Sookie is finally told what all of it was for. Bill's secret project is a database of the vampires of the world, their identities, their histories and their weaknesses, compiled at the order of the Queen of Louisiana. It is worth a kidnapping and a war, which is why Russell Edgington took him. Sookie has the only copy, retrieved and hidden where nobody else can reach it, and she declines to hand it over on request. The Mississippi business is closed the way vampire politics closes: negotiated between rulers, with Russell Edgington still on his throne and Eric's territorial insult paid for. Bill is alive and healing, and Sookie has to decide what remains between them after the trunk, and after Lorena.

Sookie ends the relationship. Bill had been planning to leave her for the vampire who made him before he was ever taken, he kept the work that endangered them both secret from her, and he nearly killed her in the trunk. She keeps the database rather than surrender it, which makes her a person the Queen of Louisiana has to deal with instead of a human who can simply be taken from. She goes home to Bon Temps, to her house and her job at Merlotte's, badly hurt and no longer anybody's girlfriend. Eric, who spent the whole affair in Jackson under an assumed name looking after her and paid for it in blood, is more openly interested in her than ever, and Alcide Herveaux, now free of Debbie Pelt, is interested too. Sookie is out of Bill's world, in the sense that she has left him, and further into the supernatural world than she has ever been.

characters.description: A recently orphaned young woman with a small income, urban tastes, and firm confidence in orderly living. Rather than seek employment, she decides to stay with relatives and chooses the Starkadders of Cold Comfort Farm, where she intends to make herself useful while shaping her surroundings into something more manageable.
characters.name: Flora Poste

characters.description: Flora's prosperous London friend and temporary host. A collector and student of brassieres, she offers Flora a comfortable base while Flora considers which branch of her extended family to approach.
characters.name: Mary Smiling

characters.description: Flora's London cousin and trusted correspondent. Fond of Flora and familiar with her habit of arranging other people's affairs, he remains a link to the polished life she leaves behind for Sussex.
characters.name: Charles Fairford

characters.description: The elderly Starkadder matriarch, who remains upstairs and rules the farm through fear, obligation, and repeated reference to a disturbing sight from her childhood in the woodshed. The family treats her wishes as final.
characters.name: Ada Doom

characters.description: An ancient farm worker who meets Flora on her arrival and introduces her to the neglected routines of Cold Comfort Farm. He tends the livestock with worn equipment and treats hardship and disorder as the natural condition of life.
characters.name: Adam Lambsbreath

characters.description: Flora's cousin and the emotionally intense mistress of the Starkadder household. She is preoccupied with her handsome son Seth and receives Flora as another claimant upon a family already bound by old resentments.
characters.name: Judith Starkadder

characters.description: Judith's husband, a severe preacher whose Church of the Quivering Brethren emphasizes sin and damnation. His religious mission occupies him more than the practical future of the farm.
characters.name: Amos Starkadder

characters.description: The elder Starkadder son, suspicious of Flora and convinced that outsiders mean to take Cold Comfort Farm from him. He cares deeply about the land and its work, though he expresses that attachment through grievance and hostility.
characters.name: Reuben Starkadder

characters.description: Judith's striking younger son, whose chief interests are women and motion pictures rather than agriculture. His beauty and dramatic instincts suggest to Flora that his future may lie far from the farm.
characters.name: Seth Starkadder

characters.description: The Starkadders' dreamy, poetry-loving daughter, who roams the Sussex hills and resists the farm's confinement. She is secretly attached to Richard Hawk-Monitor but assumes the difference in their social worlds makes a future together impossible.
characters.name: Elfine Starkadder

characters.description: A young dairy worker at Cold Comfort Farm who is burdened by repeated pregnancies and given no practical information about avoiding another. Flora recognizes her situation as a solvable problem rather than an unavoidable rural fate.
characters.name: Meriam Beetle

characters.description: A forceful Starkadder cousin who lives nearby and regards Elfine as his intended partner. His possessiveness adds another obstacle to Elfine's attachment to Richard Hawk-Monitor.
characters.name: Urk

characters.description: A writer staying in the district to pursue a literary theory. He attaches himself to Flora, interprets the countryside through fashionable psychology, and assumes that his attention should interest her more than it does.
characters.name: Mr. Mybug

characters.description: The well-bred young heir whom Elfine meets on the hills. His love for her is sincere, but his family expects him to marry someone able to move confidently within their social circle.
characters.name: Richard Hawk-Monitor

recaps.ending: Flora's separate campaigns leave the Starkadders with futures beyond their inherited disorder. Amos departs to preach in America, Seth is directed toward the film world he loves, and Reuben receives secure authority over Cold Comfort Farm. Judith accepts psychiatric help instead of centering her life on Seth. Elfine is prepared for the social world of Richard Hawk-Monitor, wins his family's acceptance, and marries him. Urk and Meriam form a practical match of their own. Flora finally confronts Ada Doom during the matriarch's family gathering and persuades her that age and the old woodshed memory need not keep her upstairs; Ada leaves to enjoy travel and fashionable life in Paris. With the farm redistributed and its inhabitants launched into new lives, Flora summons Charles Fairford. He arrives by aeroplane, they acknowledge their love, and Flora flies away with him.
recaps.in_short: After her parents die, practical Flora Poste chooses to live with distant relatives at Cold Comfort Farm in Sussex. The Starkadders are dominated by Ada Doom, who stays upstairs invoking a childhood trauma in the woodshed, while the rest of the family remain trapped in religious gloom, frustrated desire, and neglected farm work. Flora treats each crisis as an organizational problem. She secures the farm for Reuben, sends preacher Amos toward a larger American audience, steers film-obsessed Seth to a studio, finds psychiatric help for Judith, and equips Meriam to control her own future. She remakes Elfine's presentation so that Elfine can marry Richard Hawk-Monitor and finally persuades Ada to abandon her room for Paris. Once Cold Comfort Farm has a workable future, Flora calls Charles Fairford, accepts their love, and leaves with him by aeroplane.

recaps.text: After the death of her parents, Flora Poste finds herself with a modest income and no wish to take ordinary employment. Staying with her friend Mary Smiling in London, she writes to various relatives and offers them the opportunity to house her. The most compelling reply comes from Judith Starkadder of Cold Comfort Farm in Sussex. Its dark hints suggest that the Starkadders owe Flora some undefined family reparation. Flora chooses them partly because the household appears to need the order and refinement she believes she can provide. She travels to the remote village of Howling and is collected for the final journey to the farm by the aged worker Adam Lambsbreath.

At Cold Comfort Farm, Flora encounters a large family governed by custom and by the unseen authority of Ada Doom. Ada remains upstairs and controls her descendants by recalling that she saw something terrible in the woodshed as a child. Judith Starkadder is consumed by emotion, her husband Amos preaches a harsh religion, Reuben expects an attempt to steal his farm, Seth pursues women and dreams of films, and Elfine escapes into poetry and the hills. The work of the farm is as disordered as its people. Flora settles into the household without accepting its belief that misery is permanent. She begins identifying each person's practical desire and quietly considers how the competing obligations might be separated.

Flora expands her survey beyond the farmhouse. She sees the fearful intensity of Amos's Church of the Quivering Brethren and recognizes that his appetite for preaching might be redirected away from the family. She also learns that Elfine loves Richard Hawk-Monitor, a young man from a socially prominent local family, while Starkadder expectations and Elfine's lack of confidence keep the match uncertain. The writer Mr. Mybug pursues Flora while advancing a theory about literary authorship, but she remains focused on the farm. Meriam Beetle's recurring pregnancies prompt direct practical advice, and Flora begins replacing vague fatalism with specific plans for the people around her.

Flora works on several futures at once. She makes clear to Reuben that she does not want the farm and encourages him to think of himself as its responsible master rather than its dispossessed victim. Seth's absorption in motion pictures becomes a possible profession instead of a private fantasy. Elfine agrees to let Flora prepare her for Richard's social circle, learning the clothes and manners needed to prevent surface differences from deciding the relationship. Flora also refuses to be distracted by Urk's claim on Elfine or Mr. Mybug's unwanted courtship. The apparent Starkadder destinies begin to look less inevitable as each plan acquires a practical route forward.

The changes Flora has arranged begin carrying members of the household away from their fixed roles. Amos is offered a far larger field for his preaching in America. Seth is connected with the motion-picture industry, where his appearance and enthusiasm have immediate value. Richard's family sees Elfine after Flora's transformation of her presentation and accepts the match, allowing the couple to move toward marriage. Reuben's place at the farm is made increasingly secure, while Judith is offered a form of treatment for the emotions she has long treated as destiny. Ada Doom remains the central obstacle: her authority and the annual family gathering can still pull everyone back into obedience.

Flora confronts Ada Doom and treats the old woodshed memory neither as a sacred mystery nor as a permanent sentence. She persuades Ada to exchange her upstairs seclusion for travel, new clothes, and life in Paris. With the matriarch's hold released, the household disperses into the futures Flora has prepared. Amos goes to preach in America, Seth enters the film world, Reuben takes charge of Cold Comfort Farm, and Judith accepts professional help. Elfine marries Richard Hawk-Monitor with his family's approval, while Urk and Meriam also form a household. The farm is left with clearer ownership and fewer inherited grievances. Having completed her reorganization, Flora sends for Charles Fairford. He arrives in his aeroplane, Flora acknowledges that she loves him, and the two leave together by air.

characters.description: Chicago's professional wizard, back from the dead and paying for it: after months of brutal recuperation at the heart of Winter, Harry begins his service as Mab's Winter Knight - the mortal enforcer of the Queen of Air and Darkness. The mantle gives him strength and endurance and whispers to him in impulses of predatory cruelty that he must fight every hour. His first assignment looks impossible even by his standards, and taking it home to Chicago means facing friends who buried him a year ago.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: The Queen of Air and Darkness, sovereign of the Winter Court - Harry's new employer. Mab oversees her Knight's recovery personally, with a regimen of daily murder attempts in place of physical therapy, and opens his service with a single command that seems designed to be impossible. Her cruelty is real, but so is a deeper pattern: Mab does nothing without purpose, and the shape of her true war is one of the book's revelations.
characters.name: Mab

characters.description: A composed, careful mortal woman assigned to oversee Harry's recovery at Arctis Tor - part physical therapist, part social handler, guiding him through the lethal etiquette of the Winter Court. Sarissa has survived years among the Sidhe by being unfailingly controlled and giving nothing away, and she treats the new Knight with the wariness of someone who has watched what the mantle does to its bearers. There is far more to her history with Winter than she offers.
characters.name: Sarissa

characters.description: Mab's daughter, the Winter Lady - the youngest of Winter's three queens, eternally young, gleefully vicious, and bored in the way only an immortal can be. Maeve greets the new Winter Knight with mockery, provocation, and malice dressed as play. She is the subject of Mab's first command to Harry, and the question of why - what a Queen of Faerie could want done about her own daughter - drives the whole book.
characters.name: Maeve

characters.description: A pizza-loving dewdrop faerie, perhaps a foot and a half tall, who has served as Harry's scout and vassal for years and commands the Za-Lord's Guard - the militia of tiny fae Harry retains at the price of regular pizza. Fierce beyond his size and devoted beyond all reason, Toot is among the first of Harry's old allies to welcome him back from the dead, entirely unbothered by the details.
characters.name: Toot-Toot

characters.description: Harry's former apprentice, still carrying the scars of the year she spent fighting a guerrilla war while Harry was dead - and the secret they share about how he died. Her talents for veils and mind magic have matured into real power. Molly's loyalty to Harry has never wavered, and when he returns needing eyes, cover, and someone who will not flinch, she steps in without being asked. Winter has touched her life before, and it is not finished with her.
characters.name: Molly Carpenter

characters.description: Harry's half-brother, a White Court vampire, keeper of the Water Beetle and one of the few people who never quite gave up on Harry's return. The years - a skinwalker's torments, Harry's death, the secret of their kinship - have left marks on him, but when Harry needs a boat, a fighter, and family, Thomas provides all three without hesitation.
characters.name: Thomas Raith

characters.description: The genius loci of the island in Lake Michigan - a vast, ancient awareness bound to the place, to which Harry bonded himself as warden two years ago. The island summons its warden home with escalating urgency, and what it has to show him reframes everything: Demonreach is not merely a stronghold, and the calm above its shores conceals what the place was actually built to do.
characters.name: Demonreach

characters.description: Formerly of Chicago PD, the city's most capable mortal defender and the person whose judgment Harry trusts most. Murphy greets Harry's return from the dead with a cop's skepticism - verify first, feel later - and then does what she always does: shows up armed. The unspoken thing between her and Harry has survived his death; whether either of them will act on it is another matter.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: The Summer Knight - once a timid, mop-haired changeling in Harry's orbit, now a seasoned warrior and the Summer Court's mortal champion. Fix owes Harry old debts and old friendship, but he serves Titania's court, and Summer's dread of what the new Winter Knight might be - or might already be compromised by - puts the two men on a collision course neither wants.
characters.name: Fix

characters.description: The Summer Lady, youngest queen of the Summer Court - once a frightened changeling waitress whom Harry helped, elevated years ago to one of the most powerful positions in Faerie. Lily has grown into her mantle's grace and authority, but she is deeply afraid of something she will only discuss in guarded terms: a corruption moving unseen through the courts, against which she believes drastic measures are justified.
characters.name: Lily

characters.description: A spirit of intellect in an enchanted skull, currently residing with Butters, holding centuries of arcane knowledge. Bob is Harry's indispensable consultant on the things nobody else will explain: the physics of immortality, the politics of Faerie, and the fine print of the Winter mantle now wired into Harry's soul. Some subjects, though, frighten even Bob into silence.
characters.name: Bob

recaps.ending: The assault on Demonreach is broken and the prison holds, but the cost is paid in queens.
